Changelog: v0.1.6.4: Stops a telemetry upload storm and the log flood it caused. Field log 2026-10-12 05:36 showed 61 distinct hand files each attempted once inside a 13-second window while the server was answering 429 - 140 of the log's 160 lines were the resulting duplicate warnings. Two independent causes. (1) No circuit breaker: the per-file .rate-until-epoch marker only prevents a second attempt at the same file, and does nothing about the other files still queued ahead of it, so each 60s scan drained the entire backlog against a server already refusing us. TelemetryUploader now holds all uploads for the duration of the rate-limit pause, extends (never shortens) it, and closes it the moment an upload succeeds. The pause arithmetic lives in a new UploadRateLimiter so it is testable without HTTP or a real clock. (2) HttpTelemetryClient re-armed its 429 log latch on every success, so a mixed 200/429 run emitted one warning per file anyway; it now re-arms on a 10-minute cooldown instead, bounding the warning rate regardless of how the server mixes responses. Note the two log-throttles that already existed covered a different message shape, so the 05:36 flood predates them. Verified by build (0 errors/0 warnings) and the full test suite; both fixes are guarded by tests proven to fail when the fix is removed.
